stem: A bag contains $5$ black balls and $2$ red balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that the two balls have the same colour is ( )
solution: There are $C(7, 2) = 21$ equally likely pairs. The pairs of the same colour number $C(5, 2) + C(2, 2) = 10 + 1 = 11$. So the probability is $\dfrac{11}{21}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once → P(same colour)

stem: A bag contains $5$ white balls and $2$ red balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that both balls are white is ( )
solution: There are $C(7, 2) = 21$ equally likely pairs, and $C(5, 2) = 10$ of them are two white balls. So the probability is $\dfrac{10}{21}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once → P(both of one colour)

stem: A bag contains $2$ blue balls and $2$ green balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that at least one of the two balls is blue is ( )
solution: Use the complement. Pairs with no blue ball: $C(2, 2) = 1$ out of $C(4, 2) = 6$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once → P(at least one of a colour) by the complement

stem: A bag contains $3$ green balls and $4$ black balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that at least one of the two balls is green is ( )

form: Two balls drawn at once → P(at least one of a colour) by the complement

stem: Four students are each assigned at random, independently and with equal probability, to one of $6$ interest groups. The probability that at least two of them are in the same group is ( )
solution: Use the complement "all four are different". Total outcomes: $6^4 = 1296$. All different: $6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 = 360$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{360}{1296} = \dfrac{13}{18}$.
form: k people, m equally likely options → P(at least two share an option)

stem: To study favourite fruits, $60$ boys and $40$ girls were surveyed. Boys: apples $10$, bananas $20$, oranges $30$. Girls: apples $10$, bananas $10$, oranges $20$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they chose different fruits is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{10}{60} \cdot \dfrac{10}{40} + \dfrac{20}{60} \cdot \dfrac{10}{40} + \dfrac{30}{60} \cdot \dfrac{20}{40} = \dfrac{3}{8}$. So P(different) $= 1 - \dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{5}{8}$.
form: Two surveyed groups (a two-way table) → P(the two chosen people chose differently)

stem: To study how people travel to work, $100$ workers in city A and $30$ workers in city B were surveyed. Workers in city A: bus $10$, subway $10$, bicycle $80$. Workers in city B: bus $5$, subway $10$, bicycle $15$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they travel in different ways is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{10}{100} \cdot \dfrac{5}{30} + \dfrac{10}{100} \cdot \dfrac{10}{30} + \dfrac{80}{100} \cdot \dfrac{15}{30} = \dfrac{9}{20}$. stem: A box contains $5$ balls of the same size: $3$ blue balls labelled $1, 2, 3$ and $2$ black balls labelled $1, 2$. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that the two balls have different colours and the probability that they have different labels are, respectively, ( )
solution: There are $C(5, 2) = 10$ equally likely pairs. There are $3 \cdot 2 = 6$ pairs with different colours, so the first probability is $\dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$. For the second event, exactly $2$ pairs share a label, one for each label that both colours carry, so the probability of different labels is $1 - \dfrac{2}{10} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.
form: Labelled balls of two colours, two drawn at once → two probabilities (colours, labels)

For the second event, there are $C(6, 2) = 15$ pairs with no ball labelled $1$, so the probability of at least one label $1$ is $1 - \dfrac{15}{28} = \dfrac{13}{28}$.

stem: A bag contains $20$ balls of the same size: yellow, green, white and red. When one ball is drawn at random, $P(\text{yellow}) = \dfrac{3}{20}$, $P(\text{white or green}) = \dfrac{4}{5}$ and $P(\text{green or red}) = \dfrac{11}{20}$. Then the probabilities of drawing a green, a white and a red ball are, respectively, ( )
solution: The four probabilities add up to $1$. So $P(\text{red}) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{20} - \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{1}{20}$. Then $P(\text{green}) = \dfrac{11}{20} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $P(\text{white}) = \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{10}$. The options use the same three numbers in different orders, so the order green, white, red decides the answer.
form: Four colours: P(one colour) and two "or" probabilities given → the three unknown probabilities

stem: A bag contains $20$ balls of the same size: white, green, black and red. When one ball is drawn at random, $P(\text{white}) = \dfrac{1}{10}$, $P(\text{black or green}) = \dfrac{7}{20}$ and $P(\text{green or red}) = \dfrac{4}{5}$. Then the probabilities of drawing a green, a black and a red ball are, respectively, ( )
solution: The four probabilities add up to $1$. So $P(\text{red}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{7}{20} = \dfrac{11}{20}$. Then $P(\text{green}) = \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{11}{20} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $P(\text{black}) = \dfrac{7}{20} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{10}$. The options use the same three numbers in different orders, so the order green, black, red decides the answer.
form: Four colours: P(one colour) and two "or" probabilities given → the three unknown probabilities

The options use the same three numbers in different orders, so the order yellow, white, green decides the answer.

stem: There are $n$ white balls and $n$ red balls, all with distinct labels. From these, $n$ balls are drawn at random one after another without replacement. Let $Q(n)$ be the probability that the colours of the drawn balls alternate (no two consecutive balls have the same colour). Which of the following is correct? ( )
solution: Compute each value by counting: $Q(1) = 1$, $Q(2) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $Q(3) = \dfrac{3}{10}$. Each further draw must change colour, so the probability shrinks as $n$ grows. Hence $Q(1) > Q(2) > Q(3)$.
form: n white and n red balls, n drawn: a probability Q(n) compared across several n

solution: Compute each value by counting: $Q(2) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $Q(3) = \dfrac{3}{10}$, $Q(4) = \dfrac{6}{35}$. Each further draw must change colour, so the probability shrinks as $n$ grows. Hence $Q(2) > Q(3) > Q(4)$.

stem: There are $n$ white balls and $n$ red balls, all with distinct labels. From these, $n$ balls are drawn at random without replacement. Let $Q(n)$ be the probability that all $n$ drawn balls have the same colour. Which of the following is correct? ( )
solution: Compute each value by counting: $Q(1) = 1$, $Q(2) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $Q(3) = \dfrac{1}{10}$. In general $Q(n) = \dfrac{2}{C(2n, n)}$, which decreases as $n$ grows. Hence $Q(1) > Q(2) > Q(3)$.
form: n white and n red balls, n drawn: a probability Q(n) compared across several n

solution: Compute each value by counting: $Q(2) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $Q(3) = \dfrac{1}{10}$, $Q(5) = \dfrac{1}{126}$. In general $Q(n) = \dfrac{2}{C(2n, n)}$, which decreases as $n$ grows. Hence $Q(2) > Q(3) > Q(5)$.

stem: There are $4$ identical balls labelled $1, 2, 3, 4$. Three balls are drawn at random one after another without replacement. Let $m$ be the average of the numbers on the first two balls and $n$ the average of the numbers on all three balls. The probability that $|m - n| > \dfrac{1}{3}$ is ( )
solution: If the three numbers are $a, b, c$ in order, then $m - n = \dfrac{a + b}{2} - \dfrac{a + b + c}{3} = \dfrac{a + b - 2c}{6}$, so the condition is $|a + b - 2c| > 2$. Counting the ordered draws that satisfy it gives $16$ out of $24$, so the probability is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.
form: Three numbered balls drawn in order: compare the mean of the first two with the mean of all three

stem: There are $5$ identical balls labelled $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$. Three balls are drawn at random one after another without replacement. Let $m$ be the average of the numbers on the first two balls and $n$ the average of the numbers on all three balls. The probability that $|m - n| < 1$ is ( )
solution: If the three numbers are $a, b, c$ in order, then $m - n = \dfrac{a + b}{2} - \dfrac{a + b + c}{3} = \dfrac{a + b - 2c}{6}$, so the condition is $|a + b - 2c| < 6$. Counting the ordered draws that satisfy it gives $52$ out of $60$, so the probability is $\dfrac{13}{15}$.
form: Three numbered balls drawn in order: compare the mean of the first two with the mean of all three

stem: A bag contains $5$ red balls and $5$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{7}{9}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{5}{9}$
The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{5}{18}$
The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{9}$
solution: There are $C(10, 2) = 45$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{7}{9}$” is correct. It is $1 - P(\text{both blue}) = 1 - \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{7}{9}$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{5}{18}$” is incorrect. The pairs are unordered, so there are $25$ such pairs out of $45$ and the probability is $\dfrac{25}{45} = \dfrac{5}{9}$. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{5}{9}$” is incorrect. That value is the probability of exactly one red ball. Adding the case of two red balls gives $\dfrac{7}{9}$. “The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{9}$” is incorrect. That value counts only the red pairs. Adding the blue pairs gives $\dfrac{4}{9}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once: which of four probabilities is correct
answer_value: The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{7}{9}$

stem: A bag contains $5$ black balls and $4$ white balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that both balls are black is $\dfrac{25}{81}$
The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{4}{9}$
The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{5}{9}$
The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{5}{6}$
solution: There are $C(9, 2) = 36$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{5}{6}$” is correct. It is $1 - P(\text{both white}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{4}{9}$” is incorrect. The value $\dfrac{4}{9}$ is the probability of the same colour. The probability of different colours is $\dfrac{5}{9}$. “The probability that both balls are black is $\dfrac{25}{81}$” is incorrect. The balls are drawn together, so there is no replacement and the probability is $\dfrac{C(5, 2)}{C(9, 2)} = \dfrac{10}{36} = \dfrac{5}{18}$. “The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{5}{9}$” is incorrect. That value is the probability of exactly one black ball. Adding the case of two black balls gives $\dfrac{5}{6}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once: which of four probabilities is correct
answer_value: The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{5}{6}$

stem: A bag contains $4$ red balls and $2$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{5}$
The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{2}{5}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{3}{5}$
The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{4}{9}$
solution: There are $C(6, 2) = 15$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{2}{5}$” is correct. There are $C(4, 2) = 6$ such pairs out of $C(6, 2) = 15$. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{3}{5}$” is incorrect. The complement of “at least one red” is “both blue”: $1 - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{14}{15}$. “The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{5}$” is incorrect. That value counts only the red pairs. Adding the blue pairs gives $\dfrac{7}{15}$. “The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{4}{9}$” is incorrect. The balls are drawn together, so there is no replacement and the probability is $\dfrac{C(4, 2)}{C(6, 2)} = \dfrac{6}{15} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once: which of four probabilities is correct
answer_value: The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{2}{5}$

stem: A bag contains $5$ black balls and $2$ white balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{11}{21}$
The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{11}{21}$
The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{10}{21}$
The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{11}{21}$
solution: There are $C(7, 2) = 21$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{11}{21}$” is correct. There are $10 + 1 = 11$ such pairs out of $21$. “The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{10}{21}$” is incorrect. That value counts only the black pairs. Adding the white pairs gives $\dfrac{11}{21}$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{11}{21}$” is incorrect. The value $\dfrac{11}{21}$ is the probability of the same colour. The probability of different colours is $\dfrac{10}{21}$. “The probability that at least one ball is black is $\dfrac{11}{21}$” is incorrect. The complement of “at least one black” is “both white”: $1 - \dfrac{1}{21} = \dfrac{20}{21}$.
form: Two balls drawn at once: which of four probabilities is correct
answer_value: The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{11}{21}$

stem: A bag contains $2$ red balls and $3$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{2}{5}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{7}{10}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{3}{5}$
The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{4}{25}$
solution: There are $C(5, 2) = 10$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{7}{10}$” is correct. It is $1 - P(\text{both blue}) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{7}{10}$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{2}{5}$” is incorrect.
